methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native targeting Hampton Roads residents signals grassroots capability-building outside traditional tech hubs, demonstrating distributed peer-network learning that could democratize AI fluency beyond NoVA's concentrated expertise.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA to boost community AI education represents institutional commitment to deep, distributed learning in a secondary metro area, potentially creating a regional hub that challenges NoVA's concentration if successfully scaled.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches AI training program for workplace professionals - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab for workplace professionals in Southwest Virginia signals intentional capability-building in a non-metro region, but success depends on whether training creates deep fluency or shallow platform adoption among local workforce.

signals.title: In the data center capital of the world, residents ask who the AI boom is helping - NBC News
signals.signal_reading: Residents questioning who benefits from NoVA's AI boom reveals that concentrated infrastructure investment doesn't automatically translate to distributed capability or community benefit, potentially deepening the metro-rural divide despite proximity to data centers.

signals.title: Residents share data center concerns with state senators during listening tour stop in Danville
signals.signal_reading: Danville residents voicing data center concerns during a listening tour indicates Southside communities are experiencing infrastructure extraction without capability-building—physical presence of AI infrastructure concentrating while local skills and benefits remain shallow or absent.
